opportunity: Ghidra has NO Itanium RTTI analyzer at all -- its RttiAnalyzer is a Microsoft-PE analyzer and its GCC class recovery is script-tier (RecoverClassesFromRTTIScript / RTTIGccClassRecoverer), never auto-analysis -- so on a stripped g++ binary it leaves the Shape vtable as DAT_00107a80. IDA Pro reconstructs _ZTV6Widget / _ZTI6Widget / _ZTS8Drawable from .rodata + .data.rel.ro alone. kuna had ZERO _ZTV / _ZTI / __class_type_info / __cxxabiv1 hits anywhere in decompiler/crates: the Itanium side was entirely absent while the MSVC side had been ported.
test_name: kuna-console verify_itaniumrtti (7 two-pass e2e assertions over a new stripped hidden-visibility fixture) + 9 hermetic unit tests + whole-binary decompile-all sweeps
inspiration: Itanium C++ ABI 2.9.5 / 2.5.2 (type_info + vtable layout); IDA Pro's GCC RTTI reconstruction. Ghidra has no equivalent analyzer -- this is NOVEL, not a port.
root_cause: Not a defect -- an absent capability. The MSVC half of C++ RTTI recovery was ported (analyzers/rtti/), the Itanium half never was, and the mechanism does not transfer: the MSVC path finds its structures by byte-pattern scan (search for `.?A`, assume `ref - 12` is a CompleteObjectLocator), while the Itanium graph has an EXACT anchor -- the dynamic relocation that points every _ZTI object's vptr word at __cxxabiv1::__{,si_,vmi_}class_type_info's vtable with addend 2*ptr. Critically, the MSVC pass's own discovery heuristic (find the vptr value the most TypeDescriptors AGREE on) recovers NOTHING on Itanium, because in a PIE or shared object that word is 0 in the file and written by the loader.

benchmark.scorer: not run -- the pass provably emits nothing on this corpus
benchmark.why_zero: libleveldb.so is built -fno-rtti: 18 _ZTV symbols in .dynsym, ZERO _ZTI, ZERO _ZTS, ZERO __cxxabiv1 relocations. No anchor exists, so the pass emits nothing. Verified by whole-binary sweep rather than asserted: leveldb -O0 stripped 3,962 functions 0 changed, leveldb -O2 stripped 919 functions 0 changed. No benchmark number is claimed.
benchmark.vtable_half_measured_and_rejected: The separable second capability -- independent vtable detection from the 18 surviving _ZTV symbols -- was measured before scoping and is a dead end on this corpus: 126 slots total, 59 relocated to __cxa_pure_virtual, 31 unrelocated header words, and every one of the remaining 36 already carries a .dynsym FUNC name. Recoverable-but-unnamed virtual methods: 0. An independent code-pointer-run scan of .data.rel.ro reports 37 runs / 231 'functions', none matching any .dynsym symbol -- on a PIE that scan measures relocation residue, which is exactly the mistyping failure mode. It is deliberately NOT in this PR.

wrongness_axis: Attaching a wrong class name / naming a non-method. Bounded structurally: (1) a candidate is rejected unless its name string demangles as _ZTS<name>; (2) every base pointer must resolve to an already-accepted typeinfo; (3) the function-symbol commit is an idempotent find_function-gated ADD, so a real .dynsym/.symtab name is never overwritten. On the probe the two exact ABI constraints (offset-to-top <= 0; >= 1 code slot) reject 4 of 4 coincidental sub-vtable candidates, all of which are base-class pointers inside other typeinfo objects.

div_row: DIV-64 (docs/history.md): `aggressive` preset carries `itaniumrtti`. The OPTION diverges from nothing (default-off; `--mode reliable` is byte-identical), but preset membership makes it the default rendering on ELF C++ with RTTI -- a default-output change that NO parity oracle can see, which is exactly why DIV-43 exists for the symmetric removal of `dwarf_lines` from the same preset. Without preset membership this would correctly carry no DIV row. #268 took DIV-63.
option_decision: A NEW option rather than widening the PE-only `rtti`. The two paths have different default-ON trajectories: the MSVC path is a byte-pattern heuristic that will plausibly stay opt-in forever, while the Itanium path is relocation-anchored and exact with a measured 0-change footprint on 14 plain-C binaries -- a real default-ON candidate once an -frtti corpus exists. Sharing one flag would chain the sound recovery to the unsound one permanently. Secondary: the two are mutually exclusive by format anyway (MSVC RTTI only in PE, Itanium only in ELF), so a shared flag buys no user simplification, and widening a shipped option silently changes what it means on ELF inputs.
notes: No stage XML: the XML <binaryimage> datatest bootstrap never produces an AnalysisOutput and cannot reach the analyzer tier (same reason cppsig / cppproto / fdeinterior / cppcallnames all use Rust integration tests). Data labels join class to kind with `_` (Shape_vptr) rather than `::` because kuna's scope splitter splits on `::` and the C printer emits a global by its LEAF name, which would render every class's vptr as a bare ambiguous `vptr`; function symbols keep `::` because a callee's qualified name IS rendered at the call site (cppcallnames, DIV-59). Deliberately out of scope and named as follow-ups: devirtualization (the slot arrays are marked read-only, which is the precondition, but nothing devirtualizes yet -- and no rival does either on a stripped binary), this->field recovery (no decompiler does it), and independent code-pointer-run vtable scanning (measured and rejected above). The pass is registered BEFORE the Go gopclntab pass so that pass keeps its documented 'appended last' contract on a Go ELF.

speed_detail.method: AS A PRESET MEMBER: baseline is the pre-PR default path (`--mode aggressive --option itaniumrtti off`), treatment is the post-PR default path (`--mode aggressive`). Interleaved, MINIMUM of 15 pairs (31 for the fire row), on a box shared with other agents.
speed_detail.interpretation: The no-fire path -- what every user pays -- is one relocation-table walk plus one symbol walk then an early return; discovery runs BEFORE any other structure is built precisely so that path stays cheap. The large-binary rows the reviewer asked for are mcount_x86_64 (896 KiB static C, 1969 symbols) at +0.24% and stripped leveldb (1546 dynamic relocations) at +0.26%. The fire row is +0.99% here vs +2.13% measured pre-preset in isolation: same work, larger denominator, because `aggressive` already runs listing/aif/funcstart_patterns.

adversarial_findings.probe: a hostile second binary: two template instantiations (Vec<int>/Vec<double>), a three-deep namespace, and an anonymous-namespace class
adversarial_findings.result: took recovery on that binary from 7 of 14 virtual methods to 14 of 14
adversarial_findings.defect_1: Template instantiations collapsed into one class: Vec<int> and Vec<double> both reduce to `Vec` under the module's name-only demangling, and because the symbol commit is an idempotent ADD the second instantiation lost the name race and every method stayed sub_<addr>, silently. Fixed by FOLDING template arguments into the identifier (Vec_int, Vec_double) with a depth-aware `::` split, rather than deleting them.
adversarial_findings.defect_2: Every TU-local class was invisible: Itanium ABI 2.9.1 prefixes an anonymous-namespace class's type-name string with `*` (compare type_infos by pointer, not by string); that byte is not part of the mangled name, so _ZTS*N12_GLOBAL__N_16HiddenE never demangled and the class was dropped entirely. Not a corner case -- an anonymous-namespace class is how most C++ spells a concrete implementation of an exported interface (leveldb's PosixEnv).

preset_membership.why: `auto` selects `aggressive` below 500 KiB (DIV-40), which is the default path for decompile-all, the kuna CLI, the web front-end and the benchmark. An off-by-default option outside that list never runs for anyone -- the state this feature was first written in.
preset_membership.measured_before: decompile-all on the shipped fixture: default (auto) 0 recovered vtable-method names, --mode aggressive 0, explicit --option itaniumrtti on 29
preset_membership.measured_after: default (auto) 29, --mode aggressive 29, --mode reliable 0 (shipped defaults unchanged by design), explicit --option 29
preset_membership.contract: The preset's own doc-comment already reads 'every off-by-default option flipped ON except v850indirectbranch and dwarf_lines', and names the format-gated no-ops (rtti/pdb = PE, objc/macho-arm64e = Mach-O, sparcstructret = SPARC) as the safe class. itaniumrtti is that same shape with a STRICTLY NARROWER firing condition: ELF, and additionally a .rela.dyn carrying __cxxabiv1 typeinfo relocations.
preset_membership.invariant_test_added: modes.rs::aggressive_carries_every_default_off_option -- the existing test only SAMPLED five representative members, so it passed whether or not a new option was ever added to the list. The new test enforces the real contract and immediately found four further default-off options in the same trap: cortexmvectors, ptrentry, tailcallentry, paramcopyhoist. Those are recorded in an explicit UNEVALUATED list rather than silently flipped -- each changes emitted C on the binaries it fires for and needs its own sweep and PR (paramcopyhoist's own catalog row already records that its flip regresses a stage assertion and was deferred).
preset_membership.loadtime_gate_table: NO entry needed in scripts/decompile.py::_LOADTIME_GATE_ENV. #268 added that table because typedepth's DWARF types are CONSUMED inside `load file`, upstream of every console `option` line. itaniumrtti computes its facts at load but COMMITS them at `read symbols` (commit_pending_analysis -> engine.rs::analysis_pass_enabled), and the script emits every `option` line before `read symbols`. Verified rather than assumed: the generated prdemo renders sub_14b8 off and shapes::Shape::vtable_2 on. The rule is now documented next to the table.
